dedupe_keys.name: nyabiheke diesel based minigrid data hourly electricity consumption of connected users in nyabiheke refugee camp rwanda 2019 practical action re4r

description: This Humanitarian Data Exchange dataset from Practical Action gives raw hourly electricity consumption from an energy monitoring exercise on the diesel-based minigrid in Nyabiheke refugee camp, Rwanda, carried out as part of a feasibility study for renewable supply. It belongs to the Renewable Energy for Refugees (RE4R) project, which aimed to build the case for renewable energy investment in humanitarian settings with refugees and host communities. Each connected user has its own Excel file of hourly data, including an office block, the UNHCR office, a cooperative bank, salons, a restaurant, a sewing cooperative and a computer lab. The monitoring covers April to August 2019; HDX lists it as a sample survey and it is free to download under CC BY, last modified in October 2020. Coverage is one camp minigrid. Caveats: the page gives no metering method or data dictionary, the period is five months, and the publishing organisation is now marked inactive on HDX. Simulation uses are load profiles of small commercial and institutional users for sizing hybrid or solar minigrids in camps. Related records: data-energy-consumption-refugees-displaced-people-mei gives modelled camp energy use at global scale.
